tasks.query: find the most specific namespace-prefix minimum-level override for a source context, matching at a dot boundary ignoring case, else default level and switch
tasks.note: LevelOverrideMap.GetEffectiveLevel scans the overrides (sorted descending so the longest prefix wins) for a context equal to, or followed by a dot after, the override key (case-insensitive), returning the override's switch; otherwise the defaults.

tasks.query: write a string as a quoted JSON literal, escaping double quotes, backslashes and control characters with unicode escapes, copying unescaped stretches in bulk
tasks.note: JsonValueFormatter.WriteQuotedJsonString scans for chars < 32, backslash or quote, writes the clean segments in bulk and escapes the rest (\n, \r, \f, \t, \uXXXX).

tasks.query: idempotently signal shutdown of the batching sink: complete the queue writer and cancel the shutdown token once under a lock, since completing twice throws
tasks.note: BatchingSink.SignalShutdown takes _stateLock and, if not already cancelled, completes the Channel writer and cancels _shutdownSignal; Dispose and DisposeAsync both call it.

tasks.query: split a setting value of the form Namespace.Type::StaticMember, optionally followed by assembly qualifiers, into a type name and a member name using a regular expression
tasks.note: SettingValueConversions.TryParseStaticMemberAccessor matches StaticMemberAccessorRegex and recombines the short type name with the trailing qualifiers into accessorTypeName plus memberName.

tasks.query: run a configuration callback against a temporary capturing WriteTo configuration and return the single sink it added, or a disposing aggregate when several were added
tasks.note: LoggerSinkConfiguration.CreateSink builds a capturing LoggerConfiguration/LoggerSinkConfiguration, runs the callback and returns sinksToWrap[0] or a DisposingAggregateSink.

tasks.query: temporarily hide all ambient LogContext enrichers by swapping in the empty stack, returning a disposable bookmark that restores the previous stack
tasks.note: LogContext.Suspend creates a ContextStackBookmark of the current stack and sets Enrichers to EnricherStack.Empty; disposing the bookmark restores it. Reset() clears without a bookmark.

tasks.query: extension method that returns a context logger carrying a property only when the given event level is enabled, otherwise returns the same logger unchanged
tasks.note: LoggerExtensions.ForContext<TValue>(this ILogger, LogEventLevel, name, value, destructure) is the only method in the class: IsEnabled(level) ? logger.ForContext(...) : logger.

tasks.query: predicate factory selecting events by SourceContext: a generic type's full name, or a string name matching itself or a namespace prefix ending at a dot
tasks.note: Matching.FromSource has two overloads (generic type, and string name/namespace prefix); both are valid answers, def_line is the first overload.

tasks.query: render a dictionary property value as square brackets holding comma-separated parenthesised key: value pairs
tasks.note: DictionaryValue.Render writes '[' then '(key: value)' pairs separated by ', ' then ']'. SequenceValue/StructureValue.Render use different layouts.

tasks.query: split the text inside a message template placeholder into property name with destructuring prefix, comma alignment and colon format, rejecting an empty alignment
tasks.note: MessageTemplateParser.TrySplitTagContent finds ':' and ',' delimiters to produce name/format/alignment and returns false for forms like '{Name,}' or '{Name,:x}'.

tasks.query: memoises tokenised format strings keyed by reference identity; very long strings bypass the store, and it is emptied wholesale once a thousand entries accumulate
tasks.note: MessageTemplateCache.Parse skips the Hashtable (ByReferenceStringComparer) for templates over 1024 chars and clears it when it reaches 1000 items.

tasks.query: runs the attached enricher inside a try/catch, reporting any failure to diagnostics, then unconditionally forwards the event to the sink without re-testing severity
tasks.note: Logger.PostLevelCheckEmit enriches with exception handling (SelfLog) then calls _sink.Emit; the level check is done by callers.

tasks.query: on release, wipes the buffer and keeps this instance as the thread's cached one unless its capacity exceeds 32768 characters, when it is closed
tasks.note: ReusableStringWriter.Dispose(bool) clears the StringBuilder and re-pools the writer in a [ThreadStatic] field unless capacity exceeds StringBuilderCapacityThreshold.

tasks.query: reflect public getters into named members, skipping indexers and repeated names via a thread-static set; getter exceptions become message text unless propagating; anonymous types untagged
tasks.note: PropertyValueConverter.CreateStructureValue reflects properties with a [ThreadStatic] seen-names set, skips 'Item' indexers, handles TargetInvocation/NotSupported exceptions and omits the type tag for compiler-generated types.

tasks.query: returns the same instance if every child comes back reference-identical; at the first change copies earlier members, rebuilds the rest and keeps the type tag
tasks.note: LogEventPropertyValueRewriter.VisitStructureValue is copy-on-write and preserves structure.TypeTag; the sequence/dictionary variants have no type tag.

tasks.query: from reflected candidates of a given name, keep those whose parameters after the first are all defaulted or supplied by name, ordered by most supplied
tasks.note: KeyValuePairSettings.SelectConfigurationMethod filters MethodInfos by name and parameter satisfiability and orders by the count of supplied argument names.

tasks.query: thread-safe severity threshold: volatile read, locked write, raising a change notification with old and new values only when the threshold actually differs
tasks.note: LoggingLevelSwitch.MinimumLevel property: getter reads the volatile field, setter locks and invokes MinimumLevelChanged only when the value changes.

tasks.query: emit one placeholder: raw source text if no value is bound; written directly without an alignment width, else buffered and padded only if shorter
tasks.note: MessageTemplateRenderer.RenderPropertyToken writes pt.RawText when the property is missing, renders directly without alignment, else buffers in a ReusableStringWriter and pads via Padding.Apply.

tasks.query: enrichers configured through a callback on a temporary setup: none returns the parent, several are grouped fail-safe, a decorator encloses them, warning if not disposable
tasks.note: LoggerEnrichmentConfiguration.Wrap (static) collects enrichers into a list; 0 -> parent config, 1 -> itself, n -> SafeAggregateEnricher; wraps with wrapEnricher and warns via SelfLog if not IDisposable. LoggerSinkConfiguration.Wrap is the sink analogue and is about sinks.

tasks.query: emits a timestamped message with up to three format arguments to the configured callback if set, bumping a telemetry counter even when diagnostics are disabled
tasks.note: SelfLog.WriteLine formats '{UtcNow:o} {format}' with up to three args, invokes _output if not null, and always increments SelfMetrics.DiagnosticsSelfLogWrites. SelfLog.SelfLogFailureListener.OnLoggingFailed is similar (counter + callback) but takes sender/kind/events/exception, not a format string with three optional arguments.

tasks.query: sink fallback chain: a failing sink's dropped events replay into the next fallback; the chain-building configuration method, the error-catching wrapper sink and the forwarding listener
tasks.note: FallbackChain reverses the configured chain and wraps each sink in a FailureListenerSink whose listener is a DelegatingLoggingFailureListener that emits dropped events into the next sink.

tasks.query: when a batch fails to send: backoff with growing intervals, dropping the batch at the retry time limit, and eventually draining the whole queue
tasks.note: MarkFailure decides drop-batch / drop-queue from the retry limit and consecutive drops, NextInterval provides the exponential backoff, and BatchingSink.DrainOnFailure empties the channel to the failure listener.

tasks.query: how string settings like write-to:Console become configuration calls: scanning assemblies for static extension methods, matching by argument name, converting strings to parameter types
tasks.note: ApplyDirectives selects and invokes the method, FindConfigurationMethods discovers candidate static methods, and SettingValueConversions.ConvertToType converts each string argument. SelectConfigurationMethod is the part that matches candidate methods by supplied argument names.

tasks.query: how the Level placeholder of an output template is rendered: abbreviated to a width like u3 or w1, cased, then padded to the requested alignment
tasks.note: Format dispatches the Level token to LevelOutputFormat.GetLevelMoniker (width/case maps, falling back to Casing.Format for plain u/w) and pads with Padding.Apply; Padding.Apply has a string and a StringBuilder overload.

tasks.query: how properties pushed onto the ambient LogContext reach later events: the enricher registered via Enrich.FromLogContext and the context routine that walks the async-local enricher stack
tasks.note: FromLogContext registers LogContextEnricher whose Enrich calls LogContext.Enrich, which iterates the AsyncLocal EnricherStack.

tasks.query: limiting destructuring depth: the configuration option that sets the maximum, and the thread-static depth counter that yields a null scalar once it is reached
tasks.note: DepthLimiter (nested in PropertyValueConverter) keeps a [ThreadStatic] depth, returns ScalarValue.Null at the maximum; the maximum comes from Destructure.ToMaximumDepth. CreatePropertyValue has two overloads in DepthLimiter; both are valid.

tasks.query: auditing versus regular logging: how the logger chooses between exception-swallowing and exception-propagating aggregate sinks, and whether filter errors propagate
tasks.note: CreateLogger uses SafeAggregateSink for WriteTo sinks and AggregateSink (rethrowing AggregateException) when audit sinks exist, and passes auditing to FilteringSink, which rethrows filter exceptions only then.

tasks.query: isolating events sent to a secondary logger: the sink copies each event and its property dictionary first so sub-logger enrichers cannot alter the original
tasks.note: SecondaryLoggerSink.Emit calls logEvent.Copy() (new properties dictionary, same template/exception/trace ids) and writes the copy to the wrapped ILogger.

tasks.query: custom destructuring transformations for a type: configuration methods wrapping delegates in a projection policy, and the policy that applies the projection and recaptures the result
tasks.note: ByTransforming/ByTransformingWhere wrap delegates in ProjectedDestructuringPolicy, whose TryDestructure projects the value and re-captures it with destructureObjects:true.

tasks.query: how byte arrays and Memory<byte> values are captured as hex text, truncated to the first sixteen bytes with a total count once over a kilobyte
tasks.note: Two sibling policies: byte[] (ByteArrayScalarConversionPolicy) and Memory<byte>/ReadOnlyMemory<byte> (ByteMemoryScalarConversionPolicy); both cap at 16 bytes beyond 1024.

gold_context.why: CreateLogger wraps the regular WriteTo sinks in it; the constructor takes the sink sequence and Emit swallows each sink's exception, which is the non-audit behaviour.
when audit sinks exist CreateLogger combines the safe sink with the audit sinks in an AggregateSink, whose Emit rethrows failures as an AggregateException.
configured filters are applied through this wrapper; CreateLogger passes the auditing flag as propagateExceptions, which only matters inside Emit's try/catch.
CreateLogger constructs it with seven positional settings (depth, string length, collection count, scalar types, dictionary types, policies, propagateExceptions); the argument order must match.
created only when overrides exist, from the overrides dictionary, the minimum level and the level switch, which CreateLogger has stored.
CreateLogger returns new(...) calling Logger's internal constructor with processor, level, switch, sink, enricher, the dispose callbacks and the override map.
the Level token is rendered by calling GetLevelMoniker(logEvent.Level, pt.Format); the u3/w1/t4 format semantics live there.

every property token's text (level, trace id, span id, new line, exception, buffered values) is written through Padding.Apply(output, text, pt.Alignment), including the StringBuilder overload used for buffered values.
the Message token delegates to it with the event's template, properties, writer, format and format provider.
the Properties token delegates to it, passing the event template and the output template so properties already referenced in either are omitted.
supplies the well-known token names (Message, Timestamp, UtcTimestamp, Level, TraceId, SpanId, NewLine, Exception, Properties) that Format dispatches on.
when a token has an alignment, Format buffers its output in a pooled writer obtained from here so the length can be measured before padding, then disposes it.
called in the catch block; its two out parameters shouldDropBatch and shouldDropQueue decide whether the current batch is cleared and DrainOnFailure runs.
supplies the delay used to create fillBatch each iteration; it grows after consecutive failures so the loop's pacing depends on it.
the loop hands _currentBatch (an IReadOnlyCollection<LogEvent>) to this method and treats any exception as a failed batch.
the loop reports Temporary and Permanent failures through it with (sender, kind, message, events, exception).
invoked from the loop when the scheduler says to drop the queue and at shutdown with ignoreShutdownSignal; it empties the channel in chunks of 1024 to the failure listener.
the fill phase awaits it; it caches the pending read task across calls when the timeout wins and returns false on timeout or cancellation, which controls when a partial batch is emitted.
builds the $switch-name to LoggingLevelSwitch dictionary that Configure later uses to resolve minimum-level:controlled-by and override directives; it throws FormatException for invalid names.
supplies the assemblies scanned for configuration methods from the using directives and always includes Serilog's own assembly.
Configure groups the callable directives per receiver type and passes the grouped calls, discovered methods, receiver object and declared switches to it.
returns the extension (plus surrogate) methods for each receiver configuration type; Configure calls it once per receiver group with the loaded assemblies.
minimum-level:override:* directives call Override(namespacePrefix, level) or Override(namespacePrefix, switch), so both overloads must stay compatible with Configure's calls.
enrich:with-property:* directives are applied through Enrich.WithProperty(name, value).

decides whether an IEnumerable is treated as a dictionary: only registered dictionary types or generic Dictionary/ReadOnlyDictionary with primitive, built-in scalar or enum keys; otherwise the value falls through to sequence handling.
multi-dimensional arrays (Rank > 1) are delegated to it, including the per-dimension collection-count cut-off.
every key, value and element is converted through _depthLimiter.CreatePropertyValue(x, destructuring), so nesting-depth accounting depends on it.
the dictionary result is a DictionaryValue built from an IEnumerable of KeyValuePair<ScalarValue, LogEventPropertyValue>; its constructor materialises the lazy MapToDictionaryElements iterator.
the result for lists and other enumerables: built from an array for small IList values, from the lazy MapToSequenceElements iterator otherwise, or SequenceValue.Empty for empty lists.
used to write the template text, rendered message, exception and property names as escaped JSON strings; it is static and takes (string, TextWriter).
each property value is serialised through _jsonValueFormatter.Format(property.Value, output).
the Renderings section is delegated to it with the grouped format-bearing property tokens; Format writes the surrounding braces and delimiters so both must agree.
when renderMessage is true, RenderedMessage comes from logEvent.MessageTemplate.Render(logEvent.Properties).
supplies Timestamp, Level, MessageTemplate, TraceId, SpanId, Exception and Properties that are written into the JSON object.
template tokens are filtered with OfType<PropertyToken>() and grouped by PropertyName where Format != null to build the Renderings section.
the method passes the template, propertyValues ?? NoPropertyValues and the out parameters to Process, which parses (via cache) and binds EventProperty[].

Process delegates the binding to this class (ConstructProperties); it is built from the PropertyValueConverter and logs to SelfLog instead of throwing on missing, extra or positional arguments, which is why BindMessageTemplate can return true with fewer properties.
Process returns EventProperty[]; BindMessageTemplate wraps each one via new LogEventProperty(p).
the public result element type; it has an internal constructor accepting an EventProperty that is used here.
the type of the out parameter parsedTemplate, which is null (NotNullWhen false) when messageTemplate is null.
the first step: its out results (name with hint, format, alignment) and false return decide which malformed tags become TextToken.
maps a leading '@' (Destructure) or '$' (Stringify) to a Destructuring value via an out parameter; ParsePropertyToken then strips that character itself.
drives validation of dotted identifiers through the ref beginIdent state; any rejected character makes the whole tag plain text.
the successful result; its constructor (propertyName, rawText, format, alignment, destructuring) fixes the argument order used here.
returned, with the raw text preserved, for every invalid or unterminated tag.
built from an AlignmentDirection and the absolute width after parsing the alignment integer (a leading '-' means left).
Clone returns new SafeAggregateEnricher(stack); the constructor materialises the enumerable into an array, so the clone is a snapshot unaffected by later pushes and pops.
the immutable linked stack passed as the IEnumerable; it enumerates from the most recently pushed enricher down, which fixes the snapshot's enrichment order.
Clone obtains the current async-local stack from it, lazily initialising it to EnricherStack.Empty when null.
the declared return type of Clone; callers can push the returned enricher into another context.
first entry of the scalar-policy array, so it takes precedence over the others for CLR primitives.
receives BuiltInScalarTypes.Concat(additionalScalarTypes) and matches by exact runtime type from a HashSet, not by assignability.
registered after the enum policy so byte[] values are converted to hex text before any structure handling.
appended after the user-supplied destructuring policies, so user policies take priority.
the second built-in destructuring policy, keeping Type and MemberInfo values scalar.
the constructor creates it with (maximumDestructuringDepth, this), so it needs the converter instance and the depth limit as configured.
